Regular meetings are held on the 4th Monday of every month at 8:00 a.m.

should  contact the  Community  Services Department via email  at

  PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361 (AB 361)

noticing each teleconference location from which a member will be participating in a public

  CORONAVIRUS DISEASE (COVID-19) ADVISORY
As a precaution to protect staff, our constituents, and appointed officials, the City is
following the State and County Health Department’s current Health Officer
recommendations to prevent and reduce transmission of COVID-19 by holding meetings
via teleconference.

Members of the public may observe and offer comment at this meeting telephonically or
otherwise electronically:

  before or during the meeting, prior to the close of public comment on an item, to
  be read by the Board Chair during public comment. Lengthy public comment may
  be summarized in the interest of time.

BOARD OF TRUSTEES REPORTS

1. CHAIRPERSON REPORT

Chairperson Domier extended a warm welcome to the new Board Members and Alternates and
shared his appreciation for their willingness to step up and serve on the Board. He added that he
believes that the new Board will continue the good work that prior Board Members have started.
He recalled that in November, he laid out five goals for 2022, of which three are completed.

Chairperson Domier highlighted that advisory body training is on the agenda today and will take a
significant amount of time. He concluded his report with a brief background of himself, which
includes a long-time resident, a career in television, and involvement in the Little League Board,
Schools Foundation Board, committee to build the Library, and San Marino Public Library
Foundation.

2. TRUSTEE REPORTS

Trustee Chien provided a brief background of herself, which includes joining the Board in 2019, a
career in the entertainment business, involvement in her son’s schools, volunteering at a hospital,
and a long-time resident.

Trustee Derry provided a brief background of herself, which includes a long-time resident, a career

Alternate Wu provided a brief background of herself, which includes growing up in the San Gabriel

3. CRAIN ART GALLERY LIAISON REPORT

Chairperson Domier noted that the Board does not have a liaison assigned yet for the Crain Art
Gallery or the Friends of the Crowell Public Library. Trustee Derry volunteered to be the liaison
for the Friends of the Crowell Public Library and Trustee Sadun volunteered to be the liaison for
the Crain Art Gallery.

4. SAN MARINO CENTER RENOVATION UPDATE REPORT

Chairperson Domier reported that the Task Force met in preparation for the City Council meeting
on June 8. He shared that at the meeting, the Council voted to approve the environmental impact
report and to accept bids from the pre-qualified contractors. He encouraged all to attend the next
meeting on July 29 at 8:30 AM, as Council will be voting to award the contract to one of the vendors,
with a goal of breaking ground in September and completion in 18-24 months after that.

ticket pricing were discussed. Director Johnson added that the fundraiser has been scheduled for
October 15 and that the Foundation has requested to close the Library that day for set up, which
will need City Council approval. Trustee Chien shared that Director Johnson has agreed to help
advertise the event in the Community Services Guide.

8. REQUEST TO CHANGE THE FORMAT OF THE MINUTES

Management Analyst Shigenaga presented the staff report. She explained that the Library Board is
the only board / commission that utilizes “summary” minutes; all others utilize “action” minutes. She
shared that “summary” minutes require a significantly greater amount of staff time to prepare, so
staff are proposing a change to “action” minutes in hopes of better utilizing staff time.

Trustee Sadun asked if the City has software to transcribe the recording of the minutes. Management
Analyst Shigenaga responded that the City does not have software and that she is the one who
currently prepares the minutes. Director Johnson added that preparing the minutes can take 6-8
hours depending on the length of the meeting. Trustee Sadun asked if the recordings of the meeting
will be available for reference if needed. City Clerk Baker explained that the video and audio
recordings are required to be kept for one year, but are normally kept longer than that. Trustee
Osegueda asked why the Library Board prepares “summary” minutes. Chairperson Domier
explained that a few Board Members had requested more details, so the transition to “summary”
minutes occurred. Trustee Sadun shared that she thinks the Board should try “action” minutes,
especially given the staffing issues, and revisit this again if needed. Alternate Wu and Alternate Wahl
agreed that the Board should try “action” minutes knowing the time demand “summary” minutes
require.

The following person(s) provided comment:

9. CALIFORNIA STATE LIBRARY REPORT

City Librarian Vera explained that the California State Library Report is an annual statistic gathering
tool for all public libraries and the data collected is used to report on the state of libraries and for
distribution of grant money. She highlighted that certain data points are auto populated by the
California State Library, like the population. She shared that the Report is not a static document
because data points collected change year over year. Director Johnson added that the Report is a
receive and file item which then goes to the City Council as a receive and file item.

10. DIRECTOR AND CITY LIBRARIAN REPORT

Director Johnson explained that the Report includes personnel, operational, and administrative
updates. She shared how staff will be welcoming the full-time Adult Services Librarian on July 5, the
recruitment for the Recreation Commission is active through Friday, and the Friends of the Library
submitted their donation of $30,000.

In the interest of time, she asked if the Board had any questions on the rest of the Report. Trustee
Sadun noticed how part-time staff are being remunerated, which is less than Starbucks, Target, etc.
She asked if the Board can comment or help brainstorm ways to attract people to commit to
working at the Library. Director Johnson responded that this can be discussed at a later meeting,
but expressed her appreciation for Trustee Sadun’s observation. Trustee Derry shared that she

SUBJECT:  DIRECTOR AND LIBRARY MANAGER REPORT

BACKGROUND

At the request of the Library Board of Trustees, the Community Services Director and Library
Manager provide a monthly report to the Crowell Public Library Board of Trustees. The report
provides relevant administrative, operational, and financial updates, as well as information on
upcoming events, marketing and communication efforts, and customer feedback.

DISCUSSION

Personnel Updates
  • Welcome, Janelle Van Hook, our new Adult Services Librarian. She joined the City on July
  5, 2022. Prior to joining the City, she spent six years working for the City of Richmond
  Public Library running the Mobile Services Department. She earned her Bachelor’s Degree
  from Cal Poly Pomona and her Master's in Library and Information Sciences from San Jose
  State. In her free time, Janelle enjoys cross stitching and crafting. One fun fact about Janelle
  is the Bookmobile she worked on at Richmond Public Library is the same one that came to
  her preschool when she was a child!

  •  Critically-low PT staffing levels continue to strain daily library operations. Staff are working
  diligently to shift available employee resources to minimize the impact on library service
  levels. As of August 1, Youth Services will have one PT Librarian and three PT Library
  Assistant positions open. This unit will consist of one FT Librarian II only. Adult Services will
  have one PT Librarian and two PT Library Assistant positions open. This unit will consist of
  one FT Librarian II and one PT Library Assistant. PT Librarian interviews are scheduled for
  July 26.

  •  A “Meet the New Librarian Team” Fall Reception - Director Johnson and Library Manager
  Vera are working with the three FT Librarians (Plumley, Torres, and Van Hook) to plan
  and announce a meet-n-greet type event that will be open to the public. The goal is to host
  a reception in October (date TBD) and introduce this new team to the community. They

   will share their plans for holiday programming, strategic goals and priorities for the
  upcoming year, and conduct a brief community engagement survey that will allow residents
  and patrons to provide feedback related to the types of programs and services they would
  like to see offered. The survey will also be available on the website and will appear in

 Operational Staff Briefings
  Adult Programs
  Huntington Nurses Health Screening
  Huntington Hospital’s Nurses’ outreach continues at Crowell Library, with patrons being
  screened for hypertension, heart disease, and diabetes. A second nurse has come on board
  so our patrons can be more quickly screened.

  iPad for Beginners
  A group of nine senior learners taught by community favorite Samuel Edison met every
  Wednesday in June to learn how to navigate their iPads. This class is designed for older
  learners to feel more comfortable using their devices, allowing them to stay connected to
  social networks and families using modern technology. This class is made possible by the
  CDBG program.

  Chinese Club
  On June 9, the Chinese Club provided a hands-on lesson on Chinese knotting. This fine art
  has its roots in antiquity and is believed to have evolved from folk art. 12 participants had
  the opportunity to make bracelets using Chinese knotting techniques.

  Chamber Music Concert
  On June 9, Paul Stein and Leticia Oaks Strong performed Simple Gifts and the Joy of Mozart
  for 45 attendees on the Schow Patio. Paul has been a member of the Los Angeles
  Philharmonic for 36 years, and Leticia Oaks Strong joined the Los Angeles Philharmonic in
  1994.

  Toastmasters Talk of the Town
  San Marino’s Toastmasters group has seen an increase in participation, with 15 people
  coming to their first and second meeting in June. The participants were offered the
  opportunity to hone their presentation and speaking skills in a supportive and convenient
  setting.

  Coffee, Tea, and Chat
  On June 24, the Library was pleased to once again partner with the United Charity
  Foundation, which offers participants opportunities to connect with their neighbors and learn
  more about the community. This program is offered in Mandarin.

  Youth Programs
  Children’s Tie Dye Blast
  On June 8, 17 children and their families joined us for a wild afternoon of tie dye crafting.
  Children unleashed their inner free spirit by creating their own tie dye flowers, seashells,
  and pencil cases. This hands-on activity is a great way to see chemistry in action, and
  promotes creativity which is a building block to critical thinking.

  Children’s Nature Art
  The beauty in nature took center stage at this family art program. Children and their
  families created artwork using natural elements such as sunlight, feathers, and fresh
  flowers.

  13 of 17
   Children’s Take & Makes
  Throughout the month of June, three children’s take & make activities were offered to give
  families the option to participate in programs safely from home. These kits were “Explore
  San Marino,” a guide with San-Marino-specific activities and tools for young adventurers to
  become tourists in their own city (27 participants); “Postcards from Camp,” a letter-
  writing kit with colored pencils, stickers, mad libs, and other supplies (19 participants); and
  “Creatures,” a DIY woodland animal bookmark and ladybug craft (30 participants).

  YA S’mores Taste Test Take & Make
  Teens were given a starter kit of ingredients to craft the s’mores recipe of their dreams,
  and enter it into a drawing to win a Starbucks gift card. The winning recipe was by Liesel
  Grace Mendoza, inspired by chocolate covered strawberries with coconut.

  Passports
  Passport Services continue to be in high demand. In the month of June, 304 passports were
  processed, which resulted in revenue of $14,896.

  Crain Art Gallery
  A reception was held for artist Dilmit Singh on June 11 from 2 – 4 PM with about 60
  people in attendance. Singh’s exhibit, titled “Light & Literature” pairs each painting with a
  literary quote.

  An exhibit of brush painting by Wang Xiali, Vice President of the American Institute of
  Chinese Painting, will be on display from July 30 – September 8. A reception for the artist
  is scheduled for July 30 from 2:30 – 4:00 PM.

Public Works / Facility Maintenance Updates

  capacity issues within the Parks & Public Works Department. Estimated completion has been

 SUBJECT:  FY 2022-23 PLANNING TIMELINE

BACKGROUND

Staff utilize an organizational tool called a “Planning Timeline” to assist with keeping track of
reoccurring and new agenda items that need to be brought to the Library Board of Trustees, and
in what month. Some items need to go to the City Council after discussion by the Board, so it is
critical that items are not forgotten or delayed. The Timeline serve as a great reminder for staff,
but it is also a valuable orientation tool. Understanding its value, staff are sharing the FY 2022-23
Planning Timeline to help familiarize and educate the Board.

DISCUSSION

Attachment I is the FY 2022-23 Planning Timeline. Items in black appear on the agenda year over
year. Items bolded and in blue have been added by request of the Board, and may not appear on
the agenda year over year. At the bottom of the document are standing items, which are those
that appear on the agenda of every regular meeting.

In addition to sharing this document as a resource and orientation for the Board, staff request
that the Board share any items that they would like discussed or reviewed in the future.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Board receive and file the FY 2022-23 Planning Timeline and
recommend items for future discussion and review.

MINUTES
  REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE SAN MARINO LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES
  MONDAY, JULY 25, 2022 AT 8:00 A.M.
  VIA TELECONFERENCE

CALL TO ORDER: Chairperson Domier called the regular meeting to order at 8:00 a.m. via
teleconference.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Chairperson Domier led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL:  PRESENT: Alternate Wu, Trustee Sadun, Trustee Osegueda, Trustee Derry,
  Trustee Chien, Chairperson Domier, and Council Member Ude

  ABSENT: Alternate Wahl

  CITY STAFF PRESENT: Community Services Director Johnson, Library
  Manager Vera, and Management Analyst Shigenaga

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

BOARD OF TRUSTEES REPORTS

1. CHAIRPERSON REPORT

Chairperson Domier shared an update on former Trustee Eldon Swanson. He also spoke about his
personal experience working on City advisory bodies.

2. TRUSTEE REPORTS

Trustee Osegueda shared an update about her recent visit to Alcatraz Library.

Trustee Sadun, Trustee Chien, Trustee Derry, and Alternate Wu did not have anything to report at
this time.

3. CRAIN ART GALLERY LIAISON REPORT

Trustee Sadun shared her appreciation for Library Assistant Lynda Lyons, that the Gallery is booked
with exhibits up until February of next year with the next exhibit featuring Wang Xiali, and a financial
update of the Gallery.

4. SAN MARINO CENTER RENOVATION UPDATE REPORT

Chairperson Domier shared an update about the San Marino Center project timeline. Council
Member Ude provided some information about the financial side of the project.

5. FRIENDS OF THE CROWELL PUBLIC LIBRARY LIAISON REPORT
Trustee Derry did not have anything to report at this time.

6. SAN MARINO PUBLIC LIBRARY FOUNDATION LIAISON REPORT
Trustee Chien shared an update about the Literary Libations event.

CEREMONIAL

7. REORGANZATION OF THE LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES BY SELECTING
  A CHAIRPERSON AND VICE CHAIRPERSON

Trustee Sadun moved, seconded by Trustee Chien, to nominate Steve Domier for Chairperson.

Motion passed by the following vote:

AYES:  Trustee Sadun, Trustee Osegueda, Trustee Derry, Trustee Chien, Chairperson
  Domier
NOES:  None
ABSTAIN:  None
ABSENT:  None

Chairperson Domier moved, seconded by Trustee Osegueda, to nominate Debra Sadun for Vice
Chairperson.

Motion passed by the following vote:

AYES:  Trustee Sadun, Trustee Osegueda, Trustee Derry, Trustee Chien, Chairperson
  Domier
NOES:  None
ABSTAIN:  None
ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

8. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Trustee Derry moved, seconded by Trustee Chien, to approve the minutes of the Library Board of
Trustees meeting of Monday, June 27, 2022.

9. DIRECTOR AND LIBRARY MANAGER REPORT

Director Johnson and Library Manager Vera presented the staff report.

Vice Chairperson Sadun moved, seconded by Trustee Osegueda, to receive and file the Director
and Library Manager Report.

Motion passed by the following vote:

AYES:  Trustee Osegueda, Trustee Derry, Trustee Chien, Vice Chairperson Sadun,
  Chairperson Domier
NOES:  None
ABSTAIN:  None
ABSENT:  None

10. FY 2022-23 PLANNING TIMELINE

Director Johnson presented the staff report.

Trustee Osegueda moved, seconded by Trustee Chien, to receive and file the FY 2022-23 Planning
Timeline.

Motion passed by the following vote:

AYES:  Trustee Osegueda, Trustee Derry, Trustee Chien, Vice Chairperson Sadun,
  Chairperson Domier
NOES:  None
ABSTAIN:  None
ABSENT:  None

11. LITERARY LIBATIONS UPDATE

Cindy Chan, Director, and Su Viswanathan, President, of the San Marino Public Library Foundation
shared an update about Literary Libations, including activities, decorations, sponsorships, and food
and beverages.

There was discussion about volunteers and COVID-19 protocols.
